skills.name: Essay types, topic selection and planning

note.text: Essay labels describe a dominant purpose. Narrative develops events; description creates a focused impression; exposition explains; argument develops a supported position. A response can use several techniques while answering a particular task. Select a manageable topic, identify a controlling idea and order supporting points. An outline is not a collection of unrelated headings. The task and teacher determine required form and length.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to choose an essay approach fitting a task and organise a focused outline. Builds on: study explanations and relevant information. Leads to: developed essays and genre-specific writing.

paper_task.prompt: Choose a school-communication essay task. State its purpose, narrow the topic and outline a controlling idea, ordered points and an example for each. Do not draft the full essay yet.
model: Task: Explain how a school club can make notices clearer. Purpose: explanation rather than an invented adventure. Focus: readers need an identifiable activity, required action and source of confirmation.

Outline: introduce a confusing notice; explain how a precise heading identifies the activity; explain how checked details support action; conclude by showing why unconfirmed details must remain labelled as provisional. Develop each point with a relevant example.
checklist: Dominant purpose: the main communicative job requested.
Manageable focus: a topic narrow enough to develop.
Controlling idea: the central relationship guiding the outline.
Planned development: ordered points with relevant support.
Use relevant original details and check sentence boundaries, agreement and spelling.
